description: We are Team PulseDeck from Macedonia. We develop technology to improve astronaut health and safety during space missions. Our system combines health monitoring, medical records, AI analysis, nutrition tracking, emergency response, and RFID identification into one platform. We build both software and hardware using programming, electronics, and robotics. We're looking for people skilled in AI, medicine, software development, and space science.
summary:
PulseDeck is an astronaut health monitoring platform designed to improve crew health and safety during long-duration space missions, where communication with Earth may be delayed or unavailable.

Instead of keeping medical information spread across different systems, PulseDeck combines health measurements, medical records, nutrition, radiation exposure, and mental health into one accessible platform.

Each astronaut has a personal Digital Twin that tracks health changes over time. The system monitors 28 health data fields, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels, sleep, stress, cortisol, physical activity, and nutrition. It also includes mood and alertness assessments to help astronauts monitor their mental wellbeing.

PulseDeck features an offline health assistant that analyzes recorded data and suggests possible next steps, alongside an optional connected AI for more detailed explanations.

An emergency system provides quick access to critical medical information and incident reporting. An ESP32-based terminal with RFID identification allows astronauts to access their profiles quickly.

Our goal is to give astronauts a clear picture of their health, help them recognize changes early, and support independent decisions when medical assistance from Earth is delayed. PulseDeck is a working prototype that is ready to be used by astronauts on board the ISS or any other space exploration mission. It can also be used on earth to track an individuals health.
details:
PulseDeck is a digital astronaut health monitoring system designed to help astronauts understand and manage their health during long-duration space missions, especially when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.

Currently, astronauts use different systems to record medical information, nutrition, radiation exposure, and other health data. PulseDeck brings this information together into one platform, making it easier to identify changes and respond to potential problems.

Our software monitors 28 health data fields, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, sleep, stress, cortisol, radiation exposure, physical activity, and nutrition. Each astronaut has a personal Digital Twin, which uses their recorded health history to show trends and changes over time. The system also includes mood and alertness assessments to help monitor mental wellbeing.

PulseDeck features an AI health assistant that analyzes recorded information, explains possible concerns, and suggests what astronauts should check next. A rule-based offline mode works without internet access, while an optional connected AI provides more detailed explanations.

We also developed an emergency reporting system that provides immediate access to critical medical information, allergies, medications, and emergency contacts. An ESP32-based terminal with an RFID reader, OLED display, and rotary encoder allows astronauts to access their personal profiles and navigate the system quickly.

We developed the platform using Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, SQLite, Arduino programming, and ESP32 hardware.

What makes PulseDeck different is its combination of physical hardware, AI assistance, medical records, mental health monitoring, and personal Digital Twins in one system. Rather than replacing NASA's existing medical equipment, our goal is to make the information it collects easier to understand and use.

During development, we considered astronaut privacy, offline operation, emergency accessibility, ease of use, and the challenges of receiving medical support far from Earth.

Our goal is to give astronauts greater independence in monitoring their health, recognize potential problems earlier, and help keep crews safe during future missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

PulseDeck is a functional educational prototype using simulated health data. Its medical analysis and hardware integration require further testing and validation before real mission use.
